taskDescription: Arrange the three steps of one PCR cycle in the correct order.

sequenceImages.imageDescription: Denaturation at 94–95 °C: double-stranded DNA separates into two single strands.
Annealing at 50–65 °C: primers bind to complementary sequences on each single strand.
Extension at 72 °C: Taq polymerase builds new complementary strands from each primer.

l10n.score: You got @score of @total points. Each PCR cycle follows denaturation → annealing → extension: high heat separates the strands, cooling lets the primers find their complementary targets, and the heat-stable Taq polymerase extends them at 72 °C. This order is non-negotiable because primers cannot bind double-stranded DNA, and Taq requires the free 3′-OH of a bound primer to begin synthesis.
